items.title: Ο Ζάμπι από το πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο στην Popaganda: Η Ελλάδα δεν είναι σαν… είναι η χώρα μου
items.titleOriginal: Ο Ζάμπι από το πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο στην Popaganda: Η Ελλάδα δεν είναι σαν… είναι η χώρα μου
items.description: Σε έναν κόσμο που συχνά επιλέγει τη σιωπή, άλλοτε από φόβο και άλλοτε από «ωχαδερφισμό», σε έναν κόσμο που υψώνει τείχη, ανάμεσα στους ανθρώπους με μοναδικό κριτήριο το χρώμα του δέρματος, την καταγωγή ή ακόμα και τη θρησκεία, ο 15χρονος Ζάμπι, από το Πακιστάν, ήρθε με περίσσιο θάρρος να φωνάξει τη δική του αλήθεια. Μας συστήθηκε στο Πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο στα Προπύλαια, όταν με περισσή…
items.descriptionOriginal: Σε έναν κόσμο που συχνά επιλέγει τη σιωπή, άλλοτε από φόβο και άλλοτε από «ωχαδερφισμό», σε έναν κόσμο που υψώνει τείχη, ανάμεσα στους ανθρώπους με μοναδικό κριτήριο το χρώμα του δέρματος, την καταγωγή ή ακόμα και τη θρησκεία, ο 15χρονος Ζάμπι, από το Πακιστάν, ήρθε με περίσσιο θάρρος να φωνάξει τη δική του αλήθεια. Μας συστήθηκε στο Πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο στα Προπύλαια, όταν με περισσή ειλικρίνεια και χωρίς ίχνος φόβου, περιέγραψε την εμπειρία του από την σχολική πραγματικότητά του στην Ελλάδα. Μέσα από την αντιρατσιστική κραυγή του, αισθανθήκαμε τις δυσκολίες που βίωσε και βιώνει στην καθημερινότητα του. Μέσα από τα λόγια του, ήρθαμε κι εμείς αντιμέτωποι με το τι σημαίνει προκατάληψη, ρατσισμός κι αποκλεισμός. Ο Ζάμπι, επέλεξε την Popaganda, για να καταθέσει την αλήθεια του, καλώντας μας να γκρεμίσουμε κάθε εμπόδιο προκατάληψης, να τον αποδεχτούμε, να τον σεβαστούμε και να τον αγαπήσουμε. Όσο για την ιστορία του, μας υπενθυμίζει το πλέον αυτονόητο. Τα δικαιώματα κάθε παιδιού και κάθε ανθρώπου πρέπει να γίνονται σεβαστά. Ο Ζάμπι στο πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο στην Αθήνα (ΤΑΤΙΑΝΑ ΜΠΟΛΑΡΗ / EUROKINISSI) Ζάμπι, ήσουν ένα από τα πρόσωπα των ημερών, μετά από όσα είπες στα Προπύλαια, στο Πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο. Πως αισθάνεσαι; Σίγουρα, δεν περίμενα να γίνει όλος αυτός ο ντόρος. Όσοι έως τώρα, μου έχουν φερθεί καλά, εδώ στην Ελλάδα, μου είπαν πως έκανα σωστά που μίλησα. Υπήρξαν όμως κι αυτοί, οι οποίοι και στο ίντερνετ, ακόμα και δάσκαλοι από το σχολείο μου, με ρωτούσαν αν εννοούσα εκείνους, όταν έκανα λόγο για ρατσισμό. Θέλω να ξεκαθαρίσω ότι τοποθετήθηκα γενικά. Αναφέρθηκα σε όλους εκείνους που με έχουν αντιμετωπίσει ρατσιστικά, τόσο εμένα, όσο και τους φίλους μου, που έχουν έρθει από το Πακιστάν. Ήθελα να το πω. Να μάθει όλη η Ελλάδα, ότι υπάρχει κόσμος που δεν είναι καλός και ευγενικός μαζί μας. Όχι ότι δεν το ξέρουν. Ότι υπάρχουν δάσκαλοι που δεν μας προσέχουν. Από την άλλη, αυτό που πονάει περισσότερο, είναι ότι όλο αυτό το διάστημα, έχω συναντήσει παιδιά, τα οποία στο παρελθόν κυρίως, αλλά και σήμερα, με έχουν κοροϊδέψει πολλές φορές, μόνο και μόνο γιατί είμαι ξένος. Όταν λες ότι σε έχουν κοροϊδέψει; Είμαι ήδη τρία χρόνια στην Ελλάδα. Σε λίγους μήνες θα γίνω 15 χρονών. Ήρθαμε με τη μητέρα μου και τον αδερφό μου, να συναντήσουμε τον πατέρα μου, ο οποίος εργάζεται εδώ 26 χρόνια. Στη χώρα μου υπάρχει πολλή φτώχεια. Αυτό που έδινε δύναμη σε εμένα και στους γονείς μου, όταν βρεθήκαμε όλοι μαζί εδώ, ήταν ότι, θα μας περίμενε ένα καλύτερο μέλλον. Οι δυσκολίες όμως ήταν και είναι πολλές. Στην αρχή, δεν γνώριζα τη γλώσσα, δεν καταλάβαινα τίποτα. Γράφτηκα στο σχολείο και τότε κάποια παιδιά με βοήθησαν να μάθω όσο μπορώ πιο γρήγορα τα ελληνικά, όμως ήταν και εκείνα που γελούσαν μαζί μου. Με φώναζαν «μαύρο», εξαιτίας του χρώματός μου και μου φερόντουσαν άσχημα. Υπάρχουν κάποιοι που το συνεχίζουν ακόμη και σήμερα. Εγώ όμως δεν τους ακούω, δεν δίνω καν σημασία. Το πρώτο διάστημα στεναχωριόμουν, κλεινόμουν στον εαυτό μου, με τον καιρό όμως έμαθα να μην με νοιάζει. Όποιος είναι να σε προσβάλλει, θα το κάνει. Έτσι πιστεύω. Είναι κρίμα όμως για τους ανθρώπους στην Ελλάδα όλο αυτό. Όταν στεναχωριόσουν το έδειχνες; Είπες ποτέ σε κάποιο παιδί: «γιατί το κάνεις»; Όχι. Δεν ήθελα να καταλάβουν ότι με πλήγωναν. Γιατί; Δεν ήθελες να φανείς αδύναμος; Ναι, αυτό. Δεν ήθελα να ξέρουν ότι μπορούσαν να με κάνουν να νιώθω άσχημα, υποτιμητικά. Ήθελα να το κρύψω. Να μη με δουν να «πέφτω». Δεν πρέπει να συμβαίνει αυτό, να πηγαίνει δηλαδή ένα παιδί στο σχολείο και να το κοροϊδεύουν για το χρώμα και τη γλώσσα που μιλάει. Διαβάστε ακόμα Όποτε συμβαίνουν αυτά τα περιστατικά σχολικού εκφοβισμού σε βάρος σου, νιώθεις ότι οι καθηγητές ή ο διευθυντής του σχολείου προσπαθούν να σε προστατεύσουν; ( Παύση)… Εεε, ναι. Με ακούει. Πολλές φορές ο διευθυντής με ακούει. Και τι σου λέει; Ότι θα μιλήσει σε αυτό το παιδί που σου έκανε μπούλινγκ; Ναι, αυτό. Αλλά μάλλον το ξεχνάει. Και όταν τον ρωτάω, μου λέει: «Ξέχασα να μιλήσω με αυτό το παιδί». Πιστεύεις αλήθεια ότι ξεχνιέται ή απλά δεν το κάνει; Δεν ξέρω… Ο διευθυντής του σχολείου το ξέρει… Μια άλλη φορά πάλι, μου είπε ότι έκανε παρατήρηση σε κάποιο παιδί που με κορόιδευε. Μπροστά μου όμως, αυτό δεν έχει συμβεί ποτέ. Ο Ζάμπι στο πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο στην Αθήνα (ΤΑΤΙΑΝΑ ΜΠΟΛΑΡΗ / EUROKINISSI) Πέρα από τις δυσκολίες, έχεις καταφέρει να κάνεις φίλους; Ο κολλητός μου είναι ο Γιούσεφ. Με αυτόν πήγα στη συγκέντρωση, στο κέντρο και με κάποια άλλα παιδιά. Μου είπε: «Ζάμπι πρέπει να πάμε, για όλα αυτά που συμβαίνουν στη Γαλλία» Ξέρεις τι συμβαίνει στη Γαλλία; Ναι ξέρω. Τα σχολεία είναι χάλια, τα παιδιά βγαίνουν στον δρόμο, τα χτυπούν. Κι εκεί ξέρω ότι υπάρχει ρατσισμός. Όπως κι εδώ. Παντού υπάρχει, δυστυχώς. Επίσης και στο σχολείο που πηγαίνω, υπάρχουν προβλήματα. Όπως και στη Γαλλία. Οι τουαλέτες βρωμάνε, δεν έχουμε χαρτιά, μερικά τζάμια είναι σπασμένα. Αλλά για μένα το βασικότερο είναι ο ρατσισμός. Και να σας πω κάτι, όταν μίλησα στη συγκέντρωση, δεν εννοούσα μόνο το σχολείο μου, αναφέρθηκα σε όλα τα σχολεία της Ελλάδας. Παρ΄ όλα αυτά, σου αρέσει η Ελλάδα; Την αγαπάς; Ναι. Είναι η χώρα μου η Ελλάδα. Όχι σαν, είναι η χώρα μου. Εδώ μένω και εδώ θέλω να μείνω. Γι’ αυτό πήγα και στην πορεία με τους φίλους μου. Πιστεύεις ότι το κράτος μπορεί να προστατέψει παιδιά σαν και εσένα; Που έχουν έρθει με τις οικογένειες τους εδώ αναζητώντας ένα καλύτερο αύριο; Δεν πιστεύω ότι μπορεί. Μάλιστα νομίζω ότι αδιαφορεί για εμάς. Εγώ όμως είμαι χαρούμενος που ζω εδώ. Η Ελλάδα είναι πολύ καλή χώρα. Τα σχολεία όμως πρέπει να γίνουν καλύτερα και εμείς τα παιδιά να βοηθήσουμε σε αυτό. Όταν ακούω ότι για όλα φταίνε οι μετανάστες, θυμώνω. Όχι δεν φταίμε για όλα εμείς. Ο Ζάμπι στο πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο στην Αθήνα (ΤΑΤΙΑΝΑ ΜΠΟΛΑΡΗ / EUROKINISSI) Ξαφνικά μια άλλη φωνή, μπερδεύεται με αυτήν του Ζάμπι, ενώ μιλάμε στο τηλέφωνο. «Μπορώ να σας πω;», λέει ένας άντρας, που τόση ώρα προφανώς ακούει τη συζήτηση. «Είμαι ο θείος του μικρού», συμπληρώνει και ενώ μου ζητά αρχικά ευγενικά συγγνώμη για τη διακοπή, συνεχίζει: «Δεν φταίνε για όλα οι μετανάστες, να το γράψετε αυτό. Αυτή είναι μια δικαιολογία που χρησιμοποιούν οι πολιτικοί. Πριν ήταν η Χρυσή Αυγή, τώρα ακούς τον καθένα να βρίζει τους μετανάστες. Ζούμε 20 χρόνια εδώ. Δουλεύουμε σκληρά. Φέραμε στην Ελλάδα τα παιδιά μας. Δεν είμαστε παράνομοι. Κι όμως μας προσβάλλουν παντού. Ακόμα και στον δρόμο. Έχουν προσπαθήσει ακόμα και να μας χτυπήσουν. Χωρίς λόγο. Έτσι, απλά γιατί είμαστε ξένοι. Έχει τύχει να επιχειρώ να περάσω απέναντι στον δρόμο και να έρχεται κάποιος με το αυτοκίνητο του, με ταχύτητα και ενώ φταίει εκείνος, να μου φωνάζει: “Ρε Πακιστανέ τράβα στη χώρα σου”» . Ο Ιμράν, ο θείος του Ζάμπι, δίνει ξανά το τηλέφωνο στο 15χρονο αγόρι, για να ολοκληρώσουμε τη συζήτησή μας. Ζάμπι, ποια είναι τα όνειρα σου; Θέλεις να τα κάνεις πραγματικότητα μένοντας για πάντα στην Ελλάδα; Θέλω να ζήσω στην Ελλάδα για πάντα, να κάνω οικογένεια και να σπουδάσω. Αλήθεια, τι θα ήθελες να σπουδάσεις; Θέλω να γίνω δικηγόρος. Διαβάζω, προσπαθώ πολύ στο σχολείο και θα ήθελα να μπορέσω να βοηθήσω στο μέλλον τους αδύναμους. Πρέπει να σεβόμαστε ο ένας τον άλλον, ξέρετε. Γι΄ αυτό αποφάσισα να μιλήσω. Θέλω να πω σε όλα τα παιδιά στην Ελλάδα, πρώτα απ’ όλα ένα μεγάλο ευχαριστώ που με είδαν. Επίσης να ευχαριστήσω όλους εκείνους που με βοηθάνε και με σέβονται. Όλοι αδέρφια είμαστε, ξέρετε. Για μένα οι φίλοι μου, είναι αδέρφια μου. Το οξύμωρο στην περίπτωση του Ζάμπι, είναι πως, αν και από πολύ μικρός, ήρθε αντιμέτωπος με το σκληρό πρόσωπο του ρατσισμού, διατηρεί στην ψυχή του μια σπάνια καλοσύνη. Δεν αγαπά τους τσακωμούς, δεν νιώθει ισχυρός μέσα από καβγάδες και νταηλίκια, όπως ίσως άλλα παιδιά της ηλικίας του. Αντλεί απλά μια δύναμη, ακόμα κι όταν έρχεται αντιμέτωπος με ξενοφοβικές συμπεριφορέςμ να προχωρά και να ελπίζει. Να προσδοκά την ημέρα εκείνη, που δεν θα χρειάζεται να αγνοεί, μην έχοντας άλλη επιλογή, κάθε είδους ρατσιστικά σχόλια. Τη μέρα απλά, που το φαινόμενο θα εξαλειφθεί και δεν θα έχει ανάγκη να «απολογείται» για την καταγωγή του, ούτε για το χρώμα του δέρματος του. Τη μέρα που θα βρει εκείνες τις καρδιές να τον αισθανθούν και να τον καταλάβουν. Αυτός είναι ο Ζάμπι, που αν και τόσο μικρός σε ηλικία, διαθέτει ένα τεράστιο ανάστημα. Διαβάστε ακόμα The post Ο Ζάμπι από το πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο στην Popaganda: Η Ελλάδα δεν είναι σαν… είναι η χώρα μου appeared first on POPAGANDA .

items.title: Άτομα από τη Generation Jones εξηγούν τις κύριες πολιτισμικές διαφορές τους με τους Boomers
items.titleOriginal: People from Generation Jones explain their major cultural differences with Boomers
items.description: Η Generation Jones, άτομα που γεννήθηκαν από το 1954-1965, θεωρείται μια «μικρο-γενιά» μεταξύ των Boomers και της Generation X. Αν και συνήθως συγκεντρώνονται με τα Boomers, υπάρχουν μερικές αρκετά ευδιάκριτες διαφορές μεταξύ τους. Σε μια διαδικτυακή κοινότητα των Generation Jones-ers, ένα μέλος με το όνομα @WalkingHorse, παρότρυνε όσους στη Generation Jones να συζητήσουν πώς…
items.descriptionOriginal: Generation Jones , people born from 1954-1965, is considered a ‘micro-generation’ between Boomers and Generation X . Though typically lumped in with Boomers, there are some pretty distinct differences between them. In an online community of Generation Jones-ers, a member named @WalkingHorse, prompted those in Generation Jones to discuss how their upbringing differed from Boomers in a post titled “What is and who are Generation Jones. Step inside…”. “We’re often described as pragmatic idealists, raised on big dreams but tempered by economic recessions and a sense of lowered expectations compared to the Boomers’ post-war prosperity,” they wrote. “Think of us a generation that got the tail end of the party but had to clean up the mess.” So, what makes them different? It inspired many Generation Jones members to share their thoughts and opinions. These are some of the major cultural differences those in Generation Jones have with Boomers: “We were too young to fully participate in the counterculture of the ’60s but old enough to feel its aftershocks.” – @WalkingHorse Gen Jones men also signed up for the selective service, but were not drafted as the Vietnam war had ended.” – @tedshreddon “Boomers had Elvis and The Beatles. We had Led Zeppelin and Pink Floyd.” – @Scr33ble “First teenage generation to experience the Space Shuttle launch. First teen generation to watch music videos in between movies on cable TV then the birth of MTV. We laughed when hearing that golf obsessed President Gerald Ford would routinely slice or hook a ball into a crowd of spectators. Then laugh at Chevy Chase for mimicking our clumsy commander in Chief. We watched our parents go through the fuel rationing days where you could only buy gas for you car if the last digit on the plate was an odd or even number. We counted days along with the media on how long the Iran hostages were being held. We lost John Lennon while not in that sweet spot age to have experienced the musical British Invasion of the 60’s. Instead, MTV opened to floodgates to the Brit-pop invasion of Duran Duran followed closely by big hair, neon clothing and wondering why saying ‘too hip’ was all that and a bag of chips. Best part was that college tuition was sorta affordable.” – @contrivancedevice There for the start of major social change “Not mentioned yet, but we were present for the rise of gay rights. Went to my first gay bar at 19. Music, especially Disco, was infused with pride and acceptance and coming out. ‘We are Family’, ‘I’m Coming Out’. Queen and the Village People, etc. The rise of ‘women’s music’ like Holly Near and Chris Williamson. Activists like Harvey Milk and later ACT UP. We were young adults when AIDS hit and the fight for treatment led to a huge wave of coming out. We lost a whole generation of gay men to that plague. ” – @BldrJanet “Boomers remember where they were when President Kennedy died. We remember where we were when John Lennon died.” – @KJPratt “Musically speaking, I think we were blessed. Our musical heyday had everything. Our moms played Elvis the king on the radio, and we had Elvis Costello. The Stones and The Who transverse generations. We are old enough to remember Joan Baez and Bob Dylan pre-Chalamet, not to mention Freddie and Elton before their bio-pics. And Johnny Cash too. And shout out to the poster girl of the 80’s Cyndi Lauper (I got special love for her as a race tracker cause she walked hots at Belmont Park.)” – @Binky-Answer896 “We gave a hoot, and didn’t pollute!” – @Awkwardimplemet698 “We are the generation that got to see the war every evening at dinner ‘live via satellite’. – @blurtlebaby “Think: 45s—albums—-8 tracks—cassettes—-CDs—-Streaming! I’ve had the Rolling Stones on all!” – @NOLALaura “I always said that I experienced it all…born in 1957. I listened to my older siblings music. I stole my sisters Woodstock album when she went off to college. I still have it. I recall all the assassinations from JFK and MLK.I saw RFK being killed on live tv.(at least I think I did), I remember the chaos of the Vietnam war, the Chicago riots, the Nixon mess. I recall the beginning of the environmental fight, Sesame Street and the moon launch. Computers, and floppy discs, cell phones that came in small cases that would plug into the car. So much good stuff. So much chaos.” – @mammaV55 “There’s a sure way to know if you’re Gen J. Were you deadly afraid of quicksand?!” – @NOLALaura What is and who are Generation Jones. Step inside… by u/WalkingHorse in GenerationJones A generation still finding its name That’s really the throughline of every response here: a generation that grew up in the gap between two much louder cultural identities, and had to piece together its own story out of half-remembered assassinations, borrowed older siblings’ records, and a war that ended just in time to spare them but not their nerves. Boomers got Woodstock. Gen X got grunge. Generation Jones got the hangover in between, and somehow turned it into its own kind of resilience. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post People from Generation Jones explain their major cultural differences with Boomers appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Το κοριτσάκι μπήκε σε ένα talent show χωρίς να το πει στη μαμά του και το πλήθος ήταν εδώ για αυτό
items.titleOriginal: Little girl entered a talent show without telling her mom, and the crowd was here for it
items.description: Ένα κοριτσάκι μπαίνει μέσα στις καρδιές των ανθρώπων και υπενθυμίζει σε όλους μας πόσο σημαντικό είναι να βάζεις τον εαυτό σου έξω κάθε τόσο. Σε ένα πλέον viral κλιπ TikTok που δημοσιεύτηκε από τον @ashleydkennedy14, μαθαίνουμε ότι η ανιψιά της στο νηπιαγωγείο είχε προφανώς συμμετάσχει σε ένα talent show χωρίς να το πει στη μαμά της, κάτι που περιελάμβανε…
items.descriptionOriginal: One little girl is somersaulting her way into people’s hearts , and reminding us all of how important it is to put yourself out there every once in a while. In a now-viral TikTok clip posted by @ashleydkennedy14, we learn that her kindergarten-aged niece had apparently entered herself into a talent show without telling her mom, a feat that involved forging mom’s signature onto a permission slip, no less. And just what did this “act” consist of? Somersaults. Lots of ‘em. Six, to be exact. Also one cartwheel, for good measure. She’d basically deliver one roll, wait for uproarious applause, then do another one. Solid routine, if you ask us. Honestly, it’s hard to tell which aspect of this moment is more endearing: watching this little girl valiantly overcome a wee bit of shyness, and in the process tapping into some pretty captivating stage presence, or seeing how enthusiastic the audience was to support her. Just good, wholesome stuff all around. Watch: Even online viewers were taken aback by this girl’s fearlessness. Or rather, her determination to keep going, in spite of her fear. People couldn’t stop talking about it “I need to know what her parents did because this is CEO level confidence and I am here for it.” “She was like oh u like that ” “Im honestly impressed by her independence. She signed herself up and was confident that she had it. Good job mama.” “She will go far in life. Courage is everything.” Others noted how kind the crowd was to cheer her on. “For the people who clapped, as a mother : THANK YOU. it means a lottt.” “The cheers from the crowd are the best.” “Ok. because the crowd passed the vibe check. We cheer over here, be brave!” Funnily enough, plenty of other folks chimed in with similar stories of kiddos sneaking into talent shows…with talents they may or may not have actually possessed. “My son tried to sign himself up to do karate at his school talent show…he’s never been to a karate class in his life…” “My daughter entered herself into the talent show in 1st grade and didn’t say anything. She played the piano… she had never played piano in her life til that day lol I need that confidence.” “My brother did this! He played harmonica for the whole school. He doesn’t know how to play the harmonica.” The real lesson here is bigger While this girl might receive a stern talking to about the importance of not forging signatures, her story is nonetheless a prime example of how kids can really shine when left on their own to take risks, try new things, and opt for exploration over perfection. It can be hard for parents to not want to protect their little ones from failure (whatever that means), but life often provides moments just like this to remind them that taking a step back is a precious opportunity to help instill some self advocacy. It’s just like the old saying goes, “Leap, and the net will appear.” Or in this case…somersault, and the cheers will follow. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post Little girl entered a talent show without telling her mom, and the crowd was here for it appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Άτομα που γεννήθηκαν μεταξύ 1970 και ’85 ανταλλάσσουν ταμπέλες Gen X και Millennial για το «Gen Goonie»
items.titleOriginal: People born between 1970 and ’85 are trading Gen X and Millennial labels for ‘Gen Goonie’
items.description: Η Gen X (γεννημένη από το 1965 έως το 1980) αναφέρεται συχνά ως η «ξεχασμένη γενιά», επειδή βρίσκεται ανάμεσα στις πολύ μεγαλύτερες γενιές Baby Boomer και Millennial. Ωστόσο, η ετικέτα "ξεχασμένη" έχει μια ιδιαίτερη σημασία για τους νεότερους Gen Xers, καθώς ήταν πιθανότατα η λιγότερο γονεϊκή ομάδα παιδιών στην αμερικανική ιστορία. Όσοι γεννήθηκαν τη δεκαετία του 1970 ήταν…
items.descriptionOriginal: Gen X ( born 1965 to 1980 ) is often referred to as the “ forgotten generation ” because it is sandwiched between the much larger Baby Boomer and Millennial generations. However, the “forgotten” label carries a special meaning for younger Gen Xers, as they were likely the least parented group of kids in American history. Those born in the 1970s were raised in a time when more households were dual-income and the number of divorced parents was increasing. Many wore keys around their necks and took care of themselves after school. Younger Gen Xers also grew up when parents were more permissive, allowing them to stay out all day on their bikes. They only knew it was time to come home when the street lights came on. They also grew up in the last analog era without cellphones, and parents had to call around various houses to find out where their kids were. Sure, being a kid in those days was a little risky, but it also fostered a fantastic sense of independence. Where the “Gen Goonie” name comes from This experience isn’t completely limited to Gen Xers; some older millennials also experienced this type of freedom. Because kids born between 1970 and 1985 had a very specific experience, some born in this era have taken to calling themselves Generation Goonie, after the 1985 film, “ The Goonies ” starring Sean Astin, Josh Brolin, Ke Huy Quan, and Corey Feldman. “The Goonies” was a children’s movie based on a story by Steven Spielberg, with a screenplay by Chris Columbus (who would go on to direct “Home Alone”), that was directed by Richard Donner (“Superman: The Movie,” “Lethal Weapon,” “Scrooged”), who passed away in 2021. “Having been fortunate enough to speak to a lot of audiences, I have found that younger generations consider Gen X lucky to have grown up without social media and cellphones,” Chris Clews, a keynote speaker and author of ‘The Ultimate Essential Work & Life Lessons from ’80s Pop Culture,’ told Newsweek . “They often come up to me and express a desire to have grown up in an era where we knew where everyone was based on the bikes in a front yard, rather than location sharing on Snapchat.” What is Gen Goonie? “The Goonies” is a great example of the kids from this era because they lived a feral existence, traveling long distances on their bikes, had a thirst for adventure, a crude sense of humor, and an independent spirit that meant “never say die.” When their parents were on the verge of losing their homes, they didn’t wait for them to act; they went on a dangerous mission to find pirates’ treasure to prevent the developers from destroying their homes. The Goonies’ antics serve as a sharp contrast to today’s kids, who seem wrapped in bubble wrap and closely monitored by their parents. It also shows the fun kids can have when they spend time outdoors instead of on screens. The Generation Goonie trend is taking off on TikTok, where many younger Gen Xers and older millennials proudly embrace the title. For many, the moniker is more than just ‘Good Enough’ “1981, we had the best childhood out of any generation ever,” Bugface wrote. “Now this is something I’m proud to be a part of!!!!!” Rob wrote. “Hey you guys..” 77 genx here, Yorkshire, England. We definitely are the only generation of true play outside, tree climbing, bike riding, respectful, no mobile phone, VHS watching kids,” 2Dogs wrote. A ‘Goonies’ sequel is in the works The fun discussion around the term “Gen Goonie” shows that the 41-year-old film has staying power. So much that Warner Bros. greenlit a sequel to the film, with Steven Spielberg attached as producer , though no director has been announced. In August, the sequel’s writer, Potsy Ponciroli, said the screenplay was nearly done. “I have turned in a first draft, which was very well received, and I’m on a second draft, and I’m about 95% done with that, so we’re moving in the right direction,” Ponciroli said, according to Deadline . There’s nothing wrong with people who want to embrace the term Gen X. But, 41 years after “The Goonies” came out in theaters, the attitudes and the independence of the kids in the movie can be seen as a great example of a time that, sadly, we can never go back to. Humanity has crossed the digital divide and taken some of the adventure out of childhood. “The Goonies” is an excellent example of what we’ve lost, and those who understand the spirit of that era should be proud to embrace the title of “Goonie.” This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post People born between 1970 and ’85 are trading Gen X and Millennial labels for ‘Gen Goonie’ appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: America is the wealthiest country in the world, but it still lacks a few things compared to other countries. Why can’t America have a high-speed rail, a healthcare system that won’t bankrupt you, or super cool toilets like they do in other parts of the world? Why are we still tipping on every meal, and why can’t you find a decent meat pie anywhere? The great American experiment has done pretty well for the past 248 years, but we still have some blind spots. It would be cool if a brave politician could one day make America truly great by poaching all the best ideas from around the world and creating the perfect country. A Redditor recently asked people on the AskReddit subforum, “What’s one interesting thing you saw in another country that made you think, ‘How does my country not have this?” The responses are a great starting point for this hypothetical leader to begin making the improvements we’ve all been dying for. Bidets? Yes, we can! French fries with gravy? Yes, we can! Beer at Burger King? Yes, we can! We compiled a list of the 15 most interesting things they have in countries that should be implemented in America, like yesterday. 15 cool things they have in other countries that we need in America 1. Cashiers can sit down “I was an exchange student in Germany during my Junior year in high school. Right before I left, I had a job as a cashier at a grocery store. When I first went shopping in Germany, I thought, ‘THEY GET TO SIT?! WHY COULDN’T I DO THAT?!’ The only place that does this in the U.S. now is Aldi, which of course is a German company.” “Corporations: ‘It’s a slippery slope. If we let cashiers sit, what’s next? The federal government will make a law that says that pregnant women get time off, and we have to give them money? Fathers get paid time off, too? We let people stay home if they’re sick, without a doctor’s note? Employees get more than 2 weeks of vacation per year? We have to pay people enough to afford both food AND housing? Where does it end?!'” 2. On-time public transport “I travelled everywhere in Japan by public transport. My Japanese was terrible, but I could get everywhere with Google Maps because of the utter reliability of the services. I turned up at the station or bus stop and caught the transport that presented itself. The train, which was 5 minutes early, was not my train. The one that was on time on the right platform was the one I needed to catch.” 3. Foot-pedal toilets “I saw something similar in Mexico City, only it was a foot pedal to activate/flush a public toilet. This operation seems so much more sanitary than using a handle to flush a toilet.” “You want two peddles: 1) to lower the seat (it should automatically lift back up unless it has a lid which auto-closes); 2) flush.” 4. Coupon crushers “In 1997, I was in Singapore and saw these things that looked like vending machines. It was a machine that you would take your empty pop can, and put it in this compartment, lift a handle to crush the can. It would then drop down into the machine. Then the machine printed out coupons for businesses in the area. I thought it was genius! I’ve never seen it anywhere else.” 5. Bidets “More Bidets, pls. My anus can only take so much tp.” “Honestly, every person who has tried it has understood why I love them so much. It’s uncomfortable at first because it’s different, but it really does leave you feeling much cleaner.” A bidet next to a toilet. Photo credit: Murat Ts./Unsplash 6. Private public restroom stalls “Public restroom stalls without the stupid gaps in between the doors, and smaller to zero gaps on the bottoms of the doors.” 7. Server buttons “In South Korea, there were buttons on the tables to signal you were ready to order, pay, whatever. It meant no pushy or hovering waitstaff and they were able to chill and relax a bit when no one needed their help.” “In Korea, they have a ‘bing-bong’ button on your table on a restaurant. If you need something, you press the button, your table number shows up on a screen by the server station, and they come over to your table. Usually, I just hold up my empty bottle or side dish and make eye contact from across the room, and they smile and bring me another one. Otherwise, the servers don’t come by and bother you during the meal. It’s so so so much better this way.” “We have this at Korean BBQ restaurants in Los Angeles.” 8. French fries with gravy “In Canada, you can get French fries with cheese and gravy.” “We have this in the US. If you’re in the Jersey/New York area they’re called Disco Fries.” Some delicious putin. Photo credit: Canva 9. Free healthcare “Basically, your medical bills are paid for by your taxes, so when you go into the hospital, the only thing that ends up costing money is the parking. The drawback can be that there is a waitlist for some surgery (except when it’s urgently needed to keep you alive), at this time, medical insurance can pay for it, but it’s still not as expensive as in America. Also, depending on the country, your medication is also a fraction of the actual cost. For example, in America a box of medication I have to take would cost me about US$600 a month, here in Australia that same medication only costs me about US $15” “Socialized medicine is only as good as the people implementing it. If it isn’t working properly, that isn’t really the concepts fault. It’s the people running it.” 10. Traffic light countdowns “In Germany, the traffic lights go from green to yellow to red like they do everywhere else, but after red, they light up red + yellow together before green. That way people have a head start getting ready to hit the gas and by the time it’s green you’re immediately moving forward. Bothers me more than it should when it just goes from red to green in other countries.” 11. The government does the taxes “Taxes filed FOR YOU, and the return just appearing in your bank account.” 12. Beer vending machines “Beer at Burger King” (One-upper!) A man using a vending machine. Photo credit: Canva 13. Attached caps “This one’s less exciting than a lot of others, but I bought a bottle of Coke in London, and when I opened it, I realized there was a little piece of plastic that held the lid to the neck of the bottle, so you don’t have to hold it. I can’t believe we don’t do that in the US. It’s such a tiny little thing, but it feels like a no brainer when you think about it.” “That is due to a new law (an EU law, but a lot of brands have done it for their UK products too). Bottle caps have to be attached to the bottle to prevent them from being littered and to help ensure that they are also recycled along with the bottle.” 14. Meat pies “America, they are just not as big a thing here as they are in other countries. I loved them in New Zealand, in fact, when I was there, they had a fast food joint called Georgie Pie that was absolutely fantastic, also bakeries everywhere, where you could get them too.” 15. Clean public toilets “Clean, modern public toilets. I’ve been to Japan a few times, and those public toilets are amazing. I need to go back to try the one-way glass wall ones. (On a side note, having been to some Japanese music festivals, it seems that they have no problem setting up mens bathrooms in a way that the women line up looking directly into the men’s bathroom. Very odd.) What's one interesting thing you saw in another country that made you think "how does my country not have this?"? by u/dr_doctorp in AskReddit So, what would you bring home? They say there’s no place like home, but sometimes other places have amenities that would make our home a whole lot better. From sitting cashiers to free healthcare to a toilet that doesn’t require holding the lid shut, it turns out “normal” looks pretty different depending on where you grew up. The good news is none of this is impossible, it’s just a matter of someone, somewhere, deciding we deserve it too. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post Americans share 15 of the coolest things they’ve seen overseas that they want here. Like, now. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men—in 2013, it affected more than 1 million men across the world. The cancer does not behave the same way in every patient, and doctors have long faced a difficult balancing act between identifying patients who will benefit from more intensive treatment and those who may do just as well without it. Treating someone more aggressively than necessary is associated with increased side effects and poorer quality of life.

items.descriptionOriginal: Pancreatic cancer is one of the most aggressive and difficult-to-treat cancers. One reason for its resistance to therapy is the dense tissue surrounding the tumor that acts as a protective barrier and suppresses the immune response. It is a complex tissue made of supporting cells, blood vessels and immune cells—the tumor microenvironment. In pancreatic cancer, this surrounding tissue accounts for up to 90% of the tumor mass.

items.descriptionOriginal: The phase 2 BESTOW clinical trial showed that tegoprubart (a novel anti-CD40L antibody therapy) was better at preserving kidney function than tacrolimus (the current standard of care) in immunosuppressive regimens in adults receiving their first kidney transplant. Kidney graft function stabilized after the first month of treatment and remained higher in tegoprubart-treated patients than in tacrolimus-treated patients at each reported time point, with a statistically significant kidney function benefit at 18 months. A recent analysis of BESTOW data found that tegoprubart also caused greater improvements in patient-reported health-related quality of life compared with tacrolimus in study participants. The findings will be presented at ASN Kidney Week 2026, Oct. 22–25.

items.descriptionOriginal: Skin-to-skin contact, the practice of a newborn being placed directly onto the mother’s or father’s chest, is considered essential — sometimes lifesaving — care for preterm infants. The World Health Organization recommends it for at least eight hours a day beginning at birth for all babies born before 37 weeks. Incubators can also be critical for these newborns, however, and yet the carefully controlled environments prevent parents from performing that crucial skin-to-skin contact. A pioneering new technology has now bridged the two forms of care, allowing parents to hold their babies to their bodies without disrupting the essential treatments they require. Children’s Memorial Hermann Hospital The Skincubator is a wearable medical tool designed for preterm infants weighing under 4.4 pounds that enables prolonged skin-to-skin contact beginning as early as the day of birth. A couple at Children’s Memorial Hermann Hospital in Houston, Texas, recently became the first in the U.S. to experience the difference it can make. For about 10 days after their twins were born in August, Tiffany Ikwuagwu and Dorian Ojemen weren’t able to hold the babies, who arrived at just 26 weeks. “This is a great invention,” Ikwuagwu, herself an obstetrician and gynecologist, said in a video from Memorial Hermann upon using the Skincubator. “I think the fact that I can help regulate the babies’ heart[s] and help the babies relax and just have that connection to them, is very special.” Added Ojemen in an interview with CNN earlier this month: “Just the fact that you can have them on your chest, you can look in their eyes, you can hold them, feel them breathe, like, that immediately makes you feel like, wow, I’m a parent.” The tech, which was developed over four years, was granted FDA Breakthrough Device designation last December. With the Skincubator, parents can relax or rest while bonding with their baby for hours at a time, taking turns with other caregivers and family members if they so choose. Infants’ arterial, umbilical, feeding, and airway tubes all remain in place. “The baby is already in their incubator, and they’re transferred from the incubator to the Skincubator while they’re in their isolate,” explained Dr. Jaclyn Ruggiero, principal investigator for an ongoing clinical trial, adding: “The baby’s medical lines and breathing tubes or breathing support are all secured to the Skincubator base. And the way the baby gets into skin-to-skin care is there’s a retractable pad under the baby, and that pad is pulled down slowly.” Children’s Memorial Hermann Hospital Skin-to-skin contact is standard practice for all babies, helping to stabilize their heart rate and breathing, stimulating digestion, regulating temperature, providing protection against infection, and fostering the bond between parent and child. “It turns on a part of the nervous system that’s really important for connection and feeling calm,” Ruggiero said. Per the website, clinicians interested in bringing Skincubators to their NICUs can book a call with the company to begin a pilot program. Learn more. items.descriptionOriginal: Imagine walking into a lab where robots are conducting careful experiments. They are assisting researchers in the discovery of metal alloys that can snap back into shape after crumbling, or that can snake through easily into human blood vessels. ​This is not a scene from a Steven Spielberg movie or a chapter from an Isaac Asimov novel. ​It is indeed going to be a reality at the US’s Texas A&M University. The Department of Materials Science and Engineering of the university has received a $2 million grant to build a first-of-its-kind self-driven research lab, named the Aggie AI Foundry. ​Automated system test material The facility will be fully automated, equipped with artificial intelligence (AI) brainpower and robotic workers. The computer-controlled arms of the robots are expected to test novel metal alloys by mixing, melting, and testing materials based on directions from an AI brain. ​These are expected to take these laborious tasks away from humans, which still take a toll on them, and speed up the discovery and development of new metal alloys beyond current capabilities. ​”Dr. Karaman and I, along with our collaborators and students, know what it takes to design materials faster. And we have shown it,” said Raymundo Arróyave, a professor in the department. “But the process can still take a toll on humans.” ​The Foundry is a brainchild of Arróyave and Ibrahim Karaman, another materials scientist in the department. By building this lab, they hope to free the students for more creative work. ​”You want students to be creative, but imagine they are like line cooks in a big, fancy restaurant. They want to be chefs, and we have them chopping onions and cutting tomatoes. We want to free human brains and hands to conduct more science and write papers that share these discoveries with the world.” ​Trained AI brain directs robots In the lab, AI training will first take place to enable it to propose ideas for transformative alloys. These training sessions will use physical models, algorithms, and human knowledge built through years of trial and error. ​Based on the directions from the AI brain, the robotics will mix, melt, and test the materials for the desired qualities using computer-controlled robotic arms . These arms will function in the assembly line, taking samples from a wall cabinet of elements from the entire periodic table, a statement from the university read. ​These automated processes are expected to increase the rate at which metal alloys are developed from months to a week or less. ​Researchers noted that, with the current systems available, it wasn’t possible to test materials using only a computer. The work must be done on actual materials, they added. ​”The computer can predict some behavior, but there’s no computational tool anywhere in the world that can predict how an alloy is going to behave,” Arróyave said. ​But once this lab is up and running, AI can try a trillion possible ways of mixing several dozen elements from the periodic table, a feat yet not achievable for the human brain. While AI can discover hidden correlations between elements, make suggestions, and run the experiments quickly, that could fasten the pace of new alloy discoveries. ​”While it’s natural to have questions about AI, it can help scientists explore possibilities and make discoveries at a scale we’ve never seen before,” Arróyave said . ​The grant came from the WoodNext Foundation, which manages the philanthropy of tech innovator and Roku CEO and Founder Anthony Wood and his wife Susan.

items.descriptionOriginal: Most fans associate Reacher actor Alan Ritchson with kicking , punching , taking down criminals —you know, manly stuff. But the action star just revealed he also has a secret talent for singing, causing viewers to do a double take. Recently, Ritchson shared a video on his Instagram of himself singing Michael Jackson’s “Human Nature” in his hotel room (while shooting the next installment of his action-packed Amazon series). Nothing elaborate, just a backing track, a black T-shirt, and some bangin’ vocals. In his caption, he joked that the “weak attempt” was up for viewers’ pleasure or scorn. But it would quickly become clear that there would be no scorn. Fans were not prepared for Ritchson’s amazing singing voice View this post on Instagram “Calling this a weak attempt is pretty disrespectful to the rest of us who sound like injured wildlife in the shower ,” one person quipped. There were obviously more comments where that came from. On Instagram and X , people shared their shock, envy, and amazement that Ritchson had yet another special skill up his sleeve. “Bro, I’m going to call you out. You can’t be that tall, that handsome, that buff, and also have such a good voice. You need to give one up hahaha. Love your work brother,” one commenter remarked. “Remember all these buff actors used to be nerdy theatre kids. And still are lol, sing your soul dude lol,” another commenter reminisced. Actor Alan Ritchson goes viral after performing ‘Human Nature’ by Michael Jackson. pic.twitter.com/HzHPpfSjRd — Daily Loud (@DailyLoud) October 18, 2026 “Bruh had no idea this dude could sing. Was not on my bingo card this week,” commented a user. “Reacher can sing too? Some guys got handed the whole toolbox,” praised another commenter. “Reacher doing Michael Jackson is the quiet coworker who never talks in meetings and then absolutely destroys at the holiday party karaoke. Nobody looks at him the same after that,” another user noted. Newsflash: Reacher has been singing for years Of course, real ones know that Ritchson had the beginnings of a music career long before he was kicking ass onscreen. In 2004, he auditioned for American Idol in Atlanta with a flirtatious rendition of Stevie Wonder’s “You Are the Sunshine of My Life.” Earlier this year, he collaborated with artists Connor Price and Nic D on their single “Hey Heartbreaker.” And recently, he made a fan’s dream come true by filming himself singing lyrics he wrote to a piano piece they composed…all while sporting his character’s beat-up look. View this post on Instagram “Music is fun. I love music. Music makes me happy,” Ritchson wrote in the caption. It’s this enthusiasm that makes Ritchson’s abundance of gifts bearable. Do some people get an unfair amount of talent and genetic blessings? Clearly. But does it soften the blow when these people are also kind and cool to be around, and they use those blessings to share joy with others? Also yes. Now where do we sign a petition for a musical episode of Reacher ? The post ‘Reacher’ actor Alan Ritchson leaves fans stunned by hotel room rendition of Michael Jackson’s ‘Human Nature’ appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Every year, New Orleans gives thousands of discarded Christmas trees an unusual but pretty cool second life. Instead of ending up in a landfill, Louisiana National Guard helicopters fly bundled trees into the wetlands at Bayou Sauvage Urban National Wildlife Refuge. The trees support a restoration effort that helps prevent erosion, rebuild marshland, and provide habitats for local wildlife. The annual Christmas Tree Drop has been taking place for nearly three decades, bringing together New Orleans residents, local government agencies, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, and the Louisiana Army National Guard. Louisiana National Guard attaches Christmas tree bundle to helicopter. Photo Credit: USFWS How Christmas trees make it from the curb to the wetlands After the holidays, New Orleans residents leave their discarded Christmas trees at the curb for collection. The trees must be bare: no lights, ornaments, tinsel, or artificial snow can be left over since they’ll eventually become part of the natural environment. Once collected, workers secure approximately 50 to 60 trees into each bundle with wire straps. Then comes the part that makes this recycling program a little different from most. Louisiana National Guard crews attach the bundles to helicopters, with each harness holding up to four bundles at a time. The helicopters then fly over the refuge and lower the trees into designated marsh areas. According to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service , crews carefully position the bundles in straight lines to create barriers in the marsh. Once the trees are in place, refuge workers use airboats to retrieve the harnesses. It’s a fairly elaborate system for something that was sitting in someone’s living room just a month or so earlier. Louisiana National Guard harnesses tree bundle to a helicopter. Photo Credit: Louisiana Army National Guard Discarded Christmas trees are surprisingly good for the wetlands Louisiana’s wetlands play a critical role in protecting communities from flooding and storms. But erosion and other environmental pressures damage these ecosystems. When bundles of trees are placed in shallow water, their branches help slow waves and trap sediment that would otherwise be carried away. Over time, the accumulated material supports marsh grass growth, stabilizes the shoreline, and creates new habitat for birds, shrimp, crabs, and other local wildlife. A graduate student came up with the idea after wondering whether discarded Christmas trees could help rebuild marshland. It caught on, and the project became an annual restoration effort. In 2025, the City of New Orleans reported that the program had helped restore an area of marshland roughly equivalent to 330 football fields. Bayou Sauvage Refuge using a helicopter to drop a tree bundle. Photo Credit: USFWS The National Guard gets some valuable training The Christmas tree drop also provides an unexpected benefit for the Louisiana National Guard. Originally, refuge workers transported the trees using airboats. Now, National Guard helicopters transport the bundles into the wetlands, allowing crews to practice lifting and positioning heavy loads. In a 2024 Louisiana National Guard news release, Chief Warrant Officer 4 Gabriel Ruiz explained the operation benefits to the coastal environment while “also providing valuable training hours for our pilots and crew members.” Bayou Sauvage National Wildlife Refuge staff retrieve the harnesses. Photo Credit: USFWS Christmas trees have value beyond the end of January For New Orleans residents, participating doesn’t require much beyond removing decorations and placing their tree out for collection. From there, the city and its partners handle the rest. What starts as a routine holiday cleanup becomes part of a much larger effort to protect Louisiana’s wetlands. Not a bad second act for a Christmas tree most people are done with by January. The post New Orleans drops old Christmas trees into wetlands by helicopter. They’re helping rebuild the marsh. appeared first on Upworthy .

Ο Τζέφερσον Φίσερ είναι δικηγόρος στο Τέξας, ειδικός στην επικοινωνία και συγγραφέας του The Next Conversatio…
items.descriptionOriginal: In conversation, some sentences can read as condescending or, at best, annoying. Does that make sense? I wasn’t really asking there because that IS the sentence many communication experts caution against. But better, more efficient alternatives exist. Jefferson Fisher is a Texas trial lawyer, communication expert, and author of The Next Conversation . He has spent years teaching people the art of communication in a casual yet memorable (and often funny) way. With over 10 million followers across social media and podcasts, he shares plenty of insightful tips and just a few pet peeves . View this post on Instagram ‘Does that make sense?’ In an Instagram Reel , Fisher shares this pet peeve by adding a chyron to his clip that reads, “Does that make sense?” Fisher explains, “I know why you use it. You want to make sure that your words make sense, right?” The problem, he relays, is that the question doesn’t always land correctly. “That’s not what the other person hears. They hear one of two things. Either one, that you’re not really sure that they got it. So you need to make sure. So you’re like, ‘Does that make sense to your tiny brain? Because you kind of have the face of somebody who wouldn’t get it.’” This gets a laugh, as it’s clear Fisher is being playful. He adds, “Or two, you don’t really know what you’re talking about.” Try asking real questions There are better ways to go about it. “Here’s what I’m gonna ask you to do instead. Ask a real question if you truly want feedback. Like, ‘What are your thoughts? How does that feel to you? What do you think? Do you have any feedback? Do you have any questions? Cool?’” He ends, again playfully asking, ”Does that make sense?” Upworthy spoke with communications coach and author Jeff Callahan , who agrees with Fisher’s assessment. “‘Does that make sense?’ sounds polite, but it puts the other person on the spot. If they say no, they’re admitting they didn’t get it. So almost everyone says yes, whether it made sense or not. It also has the added disadvantage of making the person who says it seem less confident about themselves and their position. Instead, ask something that invites them in; my go-to is always: ‘What questions do you have?’ or ‘What thoughts or observations do you have?’ When someone’s actually engaged, they’ll show you by talking, but it’s always good to make it easy for them to jump in.” ‘Would you like more examples?’ Cassandra LeClair, PhD , also told Upworthy that the sentence is one of her biggest pet peeves, so much so that she admitted it “hit a nerve.” With a PhD in Communication Studies, she has been a professor for two decades and suggested questions she prefers instead. “What questions can I answer? Is anything sticking out to you? What resonates most for you? What can I explain more thoroughly? Would you like more examples on any of the concepts?” View this post on Instagram She adds, for context, “As a professor and speaker, my job is to convey the material. If people have questions, I should be an expert in that area. In that role, it is my job to explain things in different ways. These questions put the work back on the speaker and take away some of the shame we can feel when we are self-conscious about not understanding something.” The post Communication expert explains why people should stop asking ‘does that make sense?’ appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Anyone who has planned a vacation in the United States knows the country is huge and diverse. Each region has its own flavor; every state has its own identity, and even within a state, geographic and social diversity can vary drastically. So when mapmaker and designer Josh Barzon shared the map below and asked people which region they’d choose if they could only live and travel within one of them for the rest of their lives, people were intrigued. Take a look: You can only live & travel within one region of the United States for the rest of your life. What are you picking? pic.twitter.com/naT7HrLISk — Josh Barzon (@JoshuaBarzon) October 20, 2026 (Pay close attention to the fact that Alaska and Hawaii are included on the bottom-left of this map.) All things considered, which one would you choose? How well do people really understand the options? It might be hard to choose from these regions if you’ve never seen them yourself, and most of us haven’t seen them all. According to a 2025 YouGov poll , the average American has visited 16 states outside their home state. People in the Midwest were slightly more likely than people in other regions to have visited more than 20 states, and the older they were, the more states they had visited (which made sense). So it’s safe to say many people responding to this map prompt may not be making a fully informed decision. At least, most aren’t basing their choice on personal experience with each region. To help us understand the options a bit better, let’s briefly review each of the six regions’ major assets. The West options Starting in the West: A: California and Oregon both have some of the most stunning scenery in the country, a solid handful of nice cities, and endless nature to explore. Honestly, the Pacific coastline alone makes this one tempting for ocean lovers. Nevada and western Arizona are pretty desolate, but if you like the desert, there’s that. B: Huge nature wins in this region, especially if you like the mountains. Not a lot in the way of warm beaches, except Kaua’i got slipped into this one, which is nothing to sneeze at. Most of Alaska? Scenery galore. And don’t sleep on Washington state’s incredibly diverse (and beautiful) landscapes. C gives you a slice of everything good about America. B and the others give you some of those things, but not all of them. — Tim Lamer (@JayhawkerTim) October 20, 2026 The Rust (plus) and Bible Belt options Moving to the swooping sections that cover much of the Midwest and Atlantic coast: C: City folks and those most familiar with the East Coast might prefer this region. New York City, D.C., and Baltimore. Vacations on Cape Cod, Martha’s Vineyard, and Nantucket. Those who really love the plains and prairie states might choose this one, too. D: The Carolinas have some gorgeous coasts and nice cities that aren’t too big or too small. Tennessee has mountains and forests. Maui and Oahu—hard to beat. If you really love that part of Texas and Oklahoma, more power to you. The North-Northeast and Southeast options Finally, the smallest options land-wise, but with their own draws: E: While not quite as wild and grand as the West, the north-northeast region holds a lot of its own natural beauty. The Upper Peninsula in Michigan, Vermont, New Hampshire, Maine—lots to explore and enjoy. Chicago’s a great city. Lots of lakes in this region. Yeah man. Whole family is in Massachusetts and northern Maine is one of the nicest places in the country. I also really enjoy all 4 seasons. So, Yes, Thank you — hothamburgsandwiches (@thenewnoticer) October 20, 2026 F: Paradise for the heat lovers (and the Disney lovers). Florida Keys and the Big Island of Hawaii offer plenty of tropical delight. Austin, San Antonio, New Orleans, Miami. Do any of those descriptions change your vote? There are no right answers, but people staunchly defend their choices I have been to 40 states and lived in five of these six regions, and I found choosing one region difficult. Eliminating my last choices was pretty easy, but the top pick took serious consideration. So I was surprised to see so many people post definitive, adamant answers. I’ve seen take after take along the lines of, “How could anyone choose anything other than C?” or “B, and it’s not even close,” or “Easiest A decisions of my life.” It seems clear that every region has its benefits, and some people really love where they live. In the end, it largely boils down to what you value most in where you live and travel. I can see someone who loves the tropics choosing F, and someone who prioritizes urban living, museums, and restaurants choosing C, etc. Tough call A/B for me for those exact reasons — Smart Tech Biz (@BulldogBane) October 20, 2026 As someone obsessed with exploring natural beauty, who loves the ocean and hates humid heat, my top-to-bottom list went A, B, E, C, D, F (with D and F in a dead heat for last place). Honestly, though, I’m still vacillating between A and B for first. There’s just so much beauty in both. There are no wrong answers here. Isn’t it a gift to live in such a wildly diverse country with so much to offer? You can find more from Josh Barzon at barzondesign.com . The post A mapmaker split the U.S. randomly into 6 parts and asked people to choose. The arguments for each are fascinating. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: “Aha!” moments are great for solving problems but less so for creative judgements, according to new research. We are all familiar with the feeling of “Aha!” that accompanies the sudden realization of our next big ideas. Notably, these insights arrive with a peculiar sense of authority—you don’t just know; you know you know. Decades of research suggest this confidence is usually merited. Across anagrams, riddles, and word problems, solutions that arrive as a sudden Aha! are more likely to be correct than through step-by-step reasoning. Researchers term this finding the Eureka Heuristic, or idea that insights act as cognitive shortcuts, telling us that a given solution is likely to be correct, against our background knowledge. Crucially, past work investigated whether insights predict solution quality in problems with one, verifiable answer. But what happens when there isn’t one? UC Santa Barbara researchers Jacqueline McGuinness, Jonathan Schooler, Shelly Gable ,and Madeleine Gross posed that question in a recent featured article in the Journal of Intelligence . Their answer: in open-ended creative work, the Aha! experience is less a signal of accuracy, and more an illusory sense of brilliance—a phenomenon they refer to as the Aha! glow. “Insights tell us that an idea is promising, but primarily when there is a correct answer to be had,” says McGuinness, manager of Schooler’s META Lab in UCSB’s psychological and brain sciences department. “When we widen the solution space in creative contexts, the feeling of insight can inflate our perception of how good our ideas really are.” Evidence for the Aha! glow first comes from re-analysis of a daily diary study that tracked professional writers and physicists over two weeks. Every night, participants logged their best idea from the day, along with how creative they thought the idea was, and whether or not it came as an “Aha!” moment. Six months later, they were asked to rate the creativity of each idea again. These professions were chosen as real-world proxies for two types of problem-solving. Physicists tend to work on problems with a single, defined solution. Creative writers, in contrast, face problems where many ideas could work, and the value of each only reveals itself once fully developed. The findings revealed a striking difference between professions: writers rated their Aha! ideas as highly creative at the time of idea generation, but much lower 6-months later. On the other hand, physicists rated their Aha! ideas as more creative over time. So when an idea arrives with a flash of insight—an Aha! moment—writers come to think less of it over time, while physicists come to think more of it. Crucially, this divergence only occurred for insights; ideas arrived at through analytical reasoning improved slightly over time for both groups. A second study had 100 participants complete two laboratory tasks: a word problem task with one answer per problem, and the alternate uses task, where participants provide unusual uses for common objects like a brick or tin can. On the alternate uses task, stronger insight experiences predicted how creative people thought their ideas were, much more than creativity judgements of independent raters. Within the same participants, the association between insight intensity and idea quality was nearly four times stronger in the word problem task, compared to the creative idea generation task. “That’s the part I find illuminating,” says Schooler, a distinguished professor of psychological and brain sciences and director of UCSB’s Center for Mindfulness and Human Potential. “For the very same person the experience of aha is well-calibrated to the quality of their ideas on the one task, but produces an Aha! glow on the other.” Yet the team suspects that the glow remains useful. Across both studies, Aha! experiences also predicted greater task enjoyment, confidence, and self-reported motivation to continue working. “In creative work where there is no singular way of assessing solution quality, it often takes months or even years to assess whether an idea will be any good,” adds Gross, a project scientist in the META Lab. “So a boost of confidence, although not always warranted, might be what you need to stick with an idea long enough to find out.” In other words, the researchers say, Aha! moments in creative contexts such as the arts may be less a verdict than a motivational impetus—one that those laboring on ideas unfinished have reason to accept, even if exaggerated. Source: UC Santa Barbara The post ‘Aha!’ moments are good for problem solving, but less helpful for creative work appeared first on Futurity .

items.descriptionOriginal: People love to laugh . That’s why successful comedians make big bucks and become household names. But famous folks don’t hold all the hilarity cards. We likely all know someone in our everyday lives with a gift for comedic timing. One of those everyday improv geniuses ran into Conan O’Brien during an episode of SubwayTakes with Kareem Rahma , and people are blown away by their interaction. O’Brien is known for his ability to riff off the cuff, and this woman casually went toe-to-toe with him. Her banter even had the late-night show host belly-laughing in less than a minute, and people are raving about her. Watch: @snl sign her https://t.co/nsLVxTZp7N pic.twitter.com/UzW8x8WBuy — ktoni (@chumbwumba) October 20, 2026 How the viral bit came about The premise of the show SubwayTakes is that comedian Kareem Rahma rides the New York City subway and asks riders for their “take” on a question. Most of the people he talks to are everyday New Yorkers, but celebrities also join him. In this particular episode, Conan O’Brien spent a good 20 minutes talking to Rahma about his “5 most controversial takes,” which includes things like “All statues should be made out of soap,” and “We should have a separate area for people who want to talk about their diets.” Near the end, the comedians apologize to a woman who asks to walk between them and the camera, and she says, “That’s alright, Conan,” as she sits down next to Rahma. She said it so casually that Rahma asked if O’Brien knew the woman. That’s when the riffing started, and she didn’t drop a single ball lobbed her way. Conan himself was impressed O’Brien told Rahma that he and the woman had been married, and she immediately jumped in with, “We were married a long time ago—we got two kids.” When O’Brien asked how the kids were because he hadn’t seen them in a long time, she said, “One’s in medical school, the other one’s in jail, but he’ll be home soon.” Her deadpan delivery and commitment to the bit as it went on were simply delightful, and her quick responses had everyone giggling. “You’re amazing. What’s your name?” O’Brien asked her after their interaction. She told him her name was Debbie, and he said, “You are so funny…We got a show right here. You are absolutely fantastic.” Imagine getting that kind of compliment from Conan O’Brien! Debbie told the men she owns a bar. “Have I been thrown out of it?” O’Brien asked. Without skipping a beat, she held up two fingers and said, “Twice,” which had him rolling all over again. After a recent taping of Subway Takes, a random woman sits down and proceeds to riff with Conan O’Brien matching him joke for joke by u/EchoesOfYouth in MadeMeSmile 8 tips for being funnier Commenters across social media are saying she should be on Saturday Night Live or go into improv or stand-up comedy. Maybe she will, but there are lots of Debbies in the world who are just naturally funny people with no plans to make a career out of it. Behavioral researcher Vanessa Van Edwards says being funny is also a learnable skill, and an important one at that. She suggests eight strategies for learning to be funnier: Say yes instead of no, and vice versa If the expected answer to a question is “yes,” try saying “no” instead. Unexpected responses are a big part of humor. (You can always laugh at the surprising answer that just came out of your mouth, then give your real answer, or play with it and see what happens.) 2. Play with numbers The way Debbie said she and Conan O’Brien had “two kids” and that he’d been kicked out of her bar “twice” are perfect examples of this strategy. Specificity is funny, and numbers are an easy way to be specific. 3. Use the ‘rule of 3’ The “rule of 3” in comedy refers to a pattern: normal, normal, unexpected. Van Edwards shares examples such as “I love hot dogs, hamburgers, and handsome men” and “I am so thrilled, happy, and terrified to be here!” 4. Switch characters around Again, the idea is to set up something unexpected. For example, instead of the Big Bad Wolf being the villain, treat him as the protagonist and Little Red Riding Hood as the villain. 5. Utilize ‘whatever.’ If you find yourself the butt of a joke, pull out a “Whatever” as a surprisingly powerful way to avoid getting flustered. 6. Mine your life for stories We all have funny anecdotes from our real lives, but we often don’t think of them in the moment. Keep a running list of funny stories from your life and rehearse them regularly so you can more easily pull them out. 7. Delay the funny Don’t be too eager to share that hilarious story. Save your funny bits for the right moment. 8. Craft your own unique comedy style Embrace your quirks, draw inspiration from comedians you admire, and practice until your humor comes more naturally. We may not all be as hilarious as Conan O’Brien or Debbie, but we can all bump up our humor skills to add more laughter to a world that definitely needs it. The post A random woman on the subway went toe-to-toe with Conan O’Brien. Her quick wit had him belly-laughing. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: The oceans are in trouble. Rising temperatures due to climate change not only raise sea levels but also put enormous stress on coral reefs. When waters get too warm, healthy coral will expel the helpful algae living inside them. The coral then becomes drained of color, severely weakened, and vulnerable to disease. In other words, “ bleached coral ” is dying coral. The loss of coral and coral reefs devastates vast amounts of ocean wildlife, and humans too. So finding ways to stop, slow, or reverse coral bleaching is of major interest to scientists. And the latest breakthrough was completely unintentional. Lab studying coral encounters a “happy accident” Steve Palumbi is a professor of marine sciences at Stanford and an ocean researcher. One of his major research areas is coral, and his work recently led him to notice something pretty strange in his lab. According to Science Alert, Palumbi had collected various samples from the same coral colony when two of the samples “fell” into each other inside their tank. One was bleached, or dying, and the other was completely healthy. What’s strange is that by the time he noticed the two were touching, color had begun to return to the bleached coral, specifically at the point of contact. “I was blown away watching the actual color of this healthy coral slowly spread over into this bleached coral,” Palumbi’s fellow Stanford marine scientist Danny Collins told Science Alert . The bleaching had mysteriously reversed itself. “Helping hands” method for reviving dying coral discovered The researchers were incredibly intrigued by what they were witnessing. After further study, they realized that the healthy coral—through physical contact—was actually able to pass along some of its symbiotic algae to the unhealthy coral. Testing revealed that bleached coral could make a miraculous recovery through prolonged contact with healthy coral. Crucially, direct physical contact was the key. If the pieces of coral were even a few millimeters apart, the process didn’t work. What they observed was the two corals “fusing” together and forming a “nutrient bridge” for the algae to transfer across. Just one week of contact was sufficient to build up enough good algae on the bleached coral for it to fully recover in about seven weeks. It’s like a little life-saving hug. In the wild, bleached coral can recover if environmental conditions, such as ocean temperatures, improve. But the process often takes months, which is too slow. Most coral that gets severely bleached ends up dying during that time period. The groundbreaking method and research were recently published in Science Advances . Informally, the researchers are referring to the technique as “helping hands.” Researchers temper real-world expectations Bringing healthy coral into contact with bleached coral produced amazing results in the lab, but Stanford researchers still don’t know whether the effect can be replicated in the wild. Even if it can, it’s a process that’s likely to be slow and labor-intensive, meaning “helping hands” won’t save the oceans on their own. The technique could potentially be used in emergencies to save critically endangered reefs, but the worldwide coral reef network is going to need a lot more than that to return to its full strength. Without ocean warming stopping or reversing course, coral bleaching is likely to continue and worsen. But scientists like the Stanford team are making amazing discoveries all the time that might just help us tilt the scales. The post A random lab accident just revealed the unusual technique that can revive dying coral in weeks appeared first on Upworthy .
